subject: Hosted API — data custody, retention, and purge timelines
messages:
From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@pinecresthealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@pinecresthealth.com>

Subject: Questions on retention & emergency purge for hosted API

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Pinecrest liked the low-latency answers. Before we move to a security review, Legal and our Data Governance team asked for some concrete timelines and guarantees around three things:

1) How long customer prompt and response data is retained in the hosted API by default (both short-term cache and persistent logs).
2) What the deletion/erasure process looks like if we request a full tenant purge (timelines, affected artifacts like backups/snapshots, and verification).
3) How you handle ephemeral artifacts (KV cache, streaming buffers) and whether any persistent copies exist outside the blob storage backups.

Can you send us a concise Q&A or playbook we can include in the security questionnaire? If you have an attestation or evidence pack, please attach.

Appreciate it — Evan

Pinecrest Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention & emergency purge for hosted API

Evan —

Thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below; I attached a short playbook and a diagram that maps artifacts to retention windows. If Pinecrest needs formal evidence, we can generate an attestation PDF from our compliance portal.

Short answers (TL;DR):
- Short-term caching (KV / prefix / streaming buffers): held in-memory on serving nodes and persisted only to ephemeral local SSDs for fast restarts. Default TTL for KV cache is 1 hour; streaming buffers are discarded immediately after response commit. No long-term copies are kept in cache layers.
- Request/response logs (persistent): default retention for request/response logs is 30 days. Logs are stored in encrypted object storage and indexed for troubleshooting.
- Audit logs & metadata: audit trails (who called what API, timestamps, model version) are retained 365 days by default for customers on standard plans; enterprise customers can request longer retention or export.
- Backups & snapshots: periodic snapshots of object storage are retained for 90 days by default; snapshots are immutable and part of our disaster recovery plan. A customer-initiated purge will trigger coordinated deletion across active storage and scheduled snapshots (see playbook).

Tenant purge process (high level):
1) Customer raises a deletion request (via Console or support ticket).
2) We validate authorization and scope (tenant id, date ranges, included embeddings).
3) Active copy deletion: remove objects and metadata from live buckets and invalidate cache entries (expected < 24 hours in most cases).
4) Snapshot/safe-copy deletion: mark and schedule snapshot expiry; for immediate snapshot removal we run an expedited deletion job — typical completion within 7 calendar days, depending on snapshot size and region.
5) Verification: we produce an erasure report showing object ids deleted and a hash-based confirmation for exported artifacts. This is added to the compliance portal for your review.

Notes / constraints:
- Emergency purges can be prioritized but may incur coordination with cloud provider if objects are geo-replicated.
- Metadata indices and search traces are purged incrementally; some derived logs (for billing/chargeback) may be retained up to 90 days unless explicitly excluded.

Let me know if Legal wants specific contract language or an addendum.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Evan — quick answers and an escalation contact. Sorry for the delayed follow-up; I looped in Irene (Product Compliance) and Soojin (Platform Ops) for the snapshot detail.

A) Per-tenant retention: Yes. The request/response retention window is configurable at the tenant level via Console or via API. Options include 7, 14, 30, 90 days. Shorter windows (7 days) are common for staging environments and are supported today.

B) Expedited snapshot deletion failure modes & escalation:
- Common blockers: provider-side immutable retention policies (rare but possible if enterprise-managed retention was enabled by customer), in-flight replication to secondary region, or cross-account snapshot locks.
- Mitigations: We validate object lock settings before scheduling an expedited job; for replication in-flight we pause replication and coordinate region decommission steps.
- SLA: We offer a best-effort expedited deletion with a target completion of 7 calendar days. For Enterprise customers we can include a contractual SLA for expedited purges as part of Dedicated or Private agreements — happy to draft addendum language.

Embeddings: Transient embeddings used for routing, reranking, or short-lived store are kept in ephemeral caches by default and are not written to long-term persistent stores unless you enable "embedding persistence" in Console (off by default). If Pinecrest requires zero persistence for embeddings, we can enable a tenancy-level policy and provide an attestation.

Escalation contact (for technical purges & verification):
- Soojin Lee (Platform Ops) — soojin.lee@redwood.ai — response target 4 business hours for priority tickets.
- Irene Choi (Product Compliance) — irene.choi@redwood.ai — handles attestation and evidence packages.

Next steps:

- If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Soojin and your Security team to walk through an example purge runbook.
